chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Shazan ibn al-Khalil al-Naysaburi, from Ma'mar ibn Umar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
It suffices for the wiping upon the head to be the area of three fingers, and similarly for the leg.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of the head that must be wiped during wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the minimum valid area (rukn) for masah during wudu, specifying that wiping an area equivalent to the width of three fingers on the head and feet suffices. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes the baseline for the obligatory portion, distinguishing it from the recommended (mustahabb) practice of wiping the entire head. The extension of this measurement to the feet highlights the consistency in the physical requirements for purification across these body parts.
